subject: Hospitality
title: Labor Cost: The Other Giant
description: A 60-second lesson on Labor Cost: The Other Giant.

hook.text: Food and labor together consume 55–65% of restaurant revenue. They're called 'prime cost'—and controlling them is job number one.

buildup.text: Labor cost includes wages, benefits, taxes, training, and uniforms. A busy kitchen may have 15–20 people on payroll per shift.

discovery.text: Scheduling software uses sales forecasts to predict staffing. Over-staffing by one person per shift wastes thousands monthly.

twist.text: Cutting labor too aggressively backfires: slower service, burned-out staff, higher turnover.

climax.text: The best managers balance labor cost with service quality. Reading too many spreadsheets and not enough faces is a common mistake.

punchline.text: 55–65% goes to food and labor combined. Control both, or neither matters.

quiz.question: What is 'prime cost' in restaurant economics?
options: The cost of the best ingredients
Food cost plus labor cost combined—typically 55–65% of revenue
The price of the most popular dish
